title: HIERARCHICAL REPRESENTATION OF OPTICALLY SCANNED DOCUMENTS
abstract: Presents a hierarchical representation for optically scanned documents that preserves spatial organization and relationships among document components such as text, figures, subtitles, and captions. The representation supports recovery of logical relations including reading order.
venue: Proceedings of the Seventh International Conference on Pattern Recognition

title: Table structure recognition based on textblock arrangement and ruled line position
abstract: Early work on recognizing table structure from the arrangement of text blocks and ruled lines, addressing reconstruction of cell and table organization rather than table detection alone.

title: Recent Advances in the CLiDE Project: Logical Layout Analysis of Chemical Documents
abstract: Describes physical and logical layout analysis for chemical documents. Recognized page primitives are assigned logical roles using document-style knowledge, providing evidence for preserving semantic document structure above raw OCR and region detection.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Computer Sciences

title: A machine-learning approach for analyzing document layout structures with two reading orders
abstract: Studies document layout analysis where page elements may participate in different reading-order interpretations. It uses learned structural relationships rather than treating page segmentation as an unordered collection of boxes.

title: The Significance of Reading Order in Document Recognition and Its Evaluation
abstract: Examines reading order as a component of document recognition and discusses its representation and evaluation. It is directly relevant to preserving logical structure when converting document pages into machine-readable representations.
venue: International Conference on Document Analysis and Recognition

title: Reading order detection in visually-rich documents with multi-modal layout-aware relation prediction
abstract: Models reading order in visually rich documents through multimodal, layout-aware prediction of relations between page elements. The task goes beyond region detection by explicitly recovering structural ordering.

title: Detect-order-construct: A tree construction based approach for hierarchical document structure analysis
abstract: Addresses hierarchical document structure by detecting page objects, inferring reading order and structural relations, and constructing a document tree. It provides a representation that preserves both physical and logical organization.

title: Reading order detection on handwritten documents
abstract: Studies reading-order recovery in handwritten documents using document structure and contextual relationships. Although the domain is handwritten material rather than workplace email, the structural ordering problem is transferable to preserving document semantics.

title: LayoutLM: Pre-training of Text and Layout for Document Image Understanding
abstract: Introduces pretraining that jointly represents document text and two-dimensional layout information. The model demonstrates that spatial coordinates materially improve understanding of visually rich documents compared with text-only processing.

title: LayoutLMv2: Multi-modal Pre-training for Visually-Rich Document Understanding
abstract: Extends document pretraining to jointly use text, layout, and visual image features. Its multimodal objectives explicitly encourage alignment between textual tokens and corresponding visual regions.

title: LayoutLMv3: Pre-training for Document AI with Unified Text and Image Masking
abstract: Uses unified masking objectives across document text and page images while retaining layout information. It supports document tasks requiring joint access to textual, visual, and spatial evidence.

title: DocFormer: End-to-End Transformer for Document Understanding
abstract: Presents an end-to-end multimodal transformer that combines text, visual appearance, and spatial information for document understanding. It is relevant to preserving page structure and associations between OCR content and visual regions.

title: OCR-free Document Understanding Transformer
abstract: Introduces Donut, an OCR-free document understanding model that maps document images directly to structured textual outputs. It demonstrates an alternative to OCR pipelines but does not by itself guarantee source-region provenance for every generated value.

title: StrucTexT: Structured Text Understanding with Multi-Modal Transformers
abstract: Uses multimodal transformers to model text segments together with visual and spatial information. It targets structured text understanding including entity labeling and linking, making explicit relations among document elements rather than treating text as a flat sequence.

title: BROS: A Pre-trained Language Model Focusing on Text and Layout for Better Key Information Extraction from Documents
abstract: Pretrains representations of text together with two-dimensional layout for key-information extraction. Its relevance is primarily to spatially structured extraction; fixed-schema extraction results should not be interpreted as proof of arbitrary document or attachment understanding.

title: Doc2Graph: a Task Agnostic Document Understanding Framework based on Graph Neural Networks
abstract: Represents document entities and their relationships as a graph and applies graph neural networks to document-understanding tasks. The graph formulation is relevant to preserving relations among regions rather than flattening document contents.

title: Unifying Vision, Text, and Layout for Universal Document Processing
abstract: Introduces a unified document model that jointly processes visual, textual, and layout information and can generate structured outputs for multiple document tasks. It provides evidence for sharing a multimodal representation across extraction and question-answering tasks.

title: DocLLM: A layout-aware generative language model for multimodal document understanding
abstract: Adds layout awareness to a generative language model for document understanding without requiring a conventional vision encoder. It targets forms, tables, and visually structured documents and is relevant to preserving spatial relationships during generative reasoning.

title: Pix2Struct: Screenshot Parsing as Pretraining for Visual Language Understanding
abstract: Pretrains a vision-language model by learning to parse screenshots into simplified HTML-like structures. The approach is transferable to document and attachment understanding because it reconstructs structured visual content rather than optimizing only navigation or clicking.

title: LayoutMask: Enhance Text-Layout Interaction in Multi-modal Pre-training for Document Understanding
abstract: Improves multimodal document pretraining by strengthening interactions between textual tokens and their spatial layout. It is relevant to preserving text-region associations needed for structured extraction and evidence localization.

title: DocVQA: A Dataset for VQA on Document Images
abstract: Introduces a large benchmark for answering natural-language questions from document images. The task requires understanding text together with document layout and visual structure, although standard answer evaluation is generally less precise than explicit bounding-box evidence grounding.

title: Document Visual Question Answering Challenge 2020
abstract: Reports the 2020 DocVQA challenge and its document-image question-answering tasks. It provides benchmark evidence for reasoning over visually structured documents but should not be interpreted as explicit source-region grounding unless a task supplies such supervision.

title: InfographicVQA
abstract: Introduces question answering over infographics where information is distributed among text, graphics, and spatial layout. The benchmark is directly relevant to multimodal page understanding and transferable to image-rich workplace attachments.

title: Hierarchical multimodal transformers for Multi-Page DocVQA
abstract: Introduces a hierarchical architecture for question answering over multi-page documents and the MP-DocVQA setting. It jointly handles page selection and answer generation, providing page-level provenance but not necessarily cell- or bounding-box-level evidence.

title: Document Understanding Dataset and Evaluation (DUDE)
abstract: Provides a document-understanding benchmark spanning varied domains and multi-page, visually rich documents. Its diversity makes it useful for testing models beyond narrowly templated forms, while its results do not establish workplace-email accuracy by themselves.

title: MMLongBench-Doc: Benchmarking Long-context Document Understanding with Visualizations
abstract: Benchmarks long-document multimodal understanding over PDFs containing text, images, charts, tables, and layout information. Questions may require locating evidence across pages, making the benchmark useful for studying cross-page reasoning and source attribution.

title: LongDocURL: a Comprehensive Multimodal Long Document Benchmark Integrating Understanding, Reasoning, and Locating
abstract: Evaluates long multimodal documents with tasks spanning understanding, reasoning, and locating. Its explicit locating component is especially relevant to systems that must return not only an answer but also where supporting evidence occurs.

title: Where is this coming from? Making groundedness count in the evaluation of Document VQA models
abstract: Argues that answer correctness alone is insufficient for document question answering and explicitly evaluates whether answers are grounded in source document evidence. The work is directly relevant to provenance requirements that demand traceable support rather than plausible answer strings.

title: M3Grounder: Mask-Based Multi-Span and Multi-Granular Grounding for Document QA
abstract: Grounds document-QA evidence using masks and supports multiple evidence spans at different granularities such as phrases, lines, and blocks. This directly addresses precise localization of source evidence rather than only producing an answer or relevant page.

title: Multi-Page Document Visual Question Answering using Self-Attention Scoring Mechanism
abstract: Studies multi-page document VQA with a mechanism for scoring and selecting relevant pages before answering. It is useful supporting evidence for cross-page reasoning, but its localization granularity is page-level rather than precise cell or region grounding.

title: TableBank: A Benchmark Dataset for Table Detection and Recognition
abstract: Introduces a large dataset derived from Word and LaTeX documents for table detection and table-structure recognition. Its recognition component makes it relevant to reconstructing tabular organization, while detection-only results are supporting rather than sufficient evidence for table understanding.

title: Image-based table recognition: data, model, and evaluation
abstract: Introduces PubTabNet and an image-to-structured-table approach that reconstructs table contents and HTML structure from document images. It also introduces a structure-aware evaluation measure, providing stronger evidence for preserving cell organization than table detection alone.

title: Robust Table Detection and Structure Recognition from Heterogeneous Document Images
abstract: Addresses both table detection and reconstruction of table structure across heterogeneous document images. The structure-recognition component is directly relevant to preserving rows, columns, and cell relationships from attachments.

title: Table Structure Recognition and Form Parsing by End-to-End Object Detection and Relation Parsing
abstract: Combines detection of document objects with relation parsing to reconstruct table and form structures. Modeling relations among elements is relevant to preserving cell associations and form organization rather than extracting isolated values.

title: Table Structure Recognition using Top-Down and Bottom-Up Cues
abstract: Combines global and local visual cues to recover table structure from document images. The task includes structural reconstruction beyond locating the table region.

title: Visual Understanding of Complex Table Structures from Document Images
abstract: Targets visually complex tables whose semantics depend on nontrivial row, column, and spanning-cell organization. It is relevant to preserving structural relations that are easily lost when tables are flattened into plain text.

title: Multi-Type-TD-TSR -- Extracting Tables from Document Images using a Multi-stage Pipeline for Table Detection and Table Structure Recognition: from OCR to Structured Table Representations
abstract: Presents a pipeline that converts document images into structured table representations through table detection and table-structure recognition. Its explicit structured output is relevant to retaining row-column relationships after extraction.

title: TUTA: Tree-based Transformers for Generally Structured Table Pre-training
abstract: Represents generally structured tables with tree-based positional and structural information and pretrains a transformer over that hierarchy. It directly addresses hierarchical headers and semantic table structure rather than treating tables as flat sequences.

title: TURL: Table Understanding through Representation Learning
abstract: Learns contextual representations for relational tables and applies them to table-understanding tasks involving entities and semantic relationships. Because its input is already structured tables, it is transferable to downstream reasoning but does not solve extraction from document images.

title: TaBERT: Pretraining for Joint Understanding of Textual and Tabular Data
abstract: Pretrains representations jointly over natural-language text and semi-structured tables. It is relevant to reasoning over tables once their structure is available, but is transfer evidence rather than evidence for recovering table structure from images or attachments.

title: TaPas: Weakly Supervised Table Parsing via Pre-training
abstract: Pretrains a model for answering questions over tables using cell selection and aggregation. It demonstrates cell-level reasoning over already normalized tables, so it is transferable to downstream evidence selection rather than direct document-table extraction.

title: SpreadsheetLLM: Encoding Spreadsheets for Large Language Models
abstract: Develops structure-aware encodings that preserve spreadsheet values, locations, formatting, and hierarchical organization while making workbooks tractable for language models. It is relevant to semantic understanding of existing spreadsheet structure and cell-addressable evidence.

title: PlotQA: Reasoning over Scientific Plots
abstract: Introduces question answering over scientific plots with questions requiring extraction and reasoning over chart values. Its chart reasoning mechanisms are transferable to workplace attachments, though synthetic aspects of the benchmark limit claims about real-world extraction robustness.

title: ChartQA: A Benchmark for Question Answering about Charts with Visual and Logical Reasoning
abstract: Introduces chart question answering that combines visual recognition with logical and arithmetic reasoning. It includes real-world charts and is relevant to understanding chart-bearing documents, though answer correctness does not itself imply precise region grounding.

title: DePlot: One-shot visual language reasoning by plot-to-table translation
abstract: Converts chart images into linearized tables that can be consumed by language models for downstream reasoning. It is relevant to preserving the data structure behind visual plots, but does not by itself provide fine-grained visual provenance for every extracted value.

title: RefChartQA: Grounding Visual Answer on Chart Images through Instruction Tuning
abstract: Extends chart question answering toward explicit visual grounding of answers in chart images. This makes it directly relevant to requirements where answers must be tied back to the chart elements or regions that support them.

title: Phrase Grounding by Soft-Label Chain Conditional Random Field
abstract: Studies phrase grounding by linking textual phrases to image regions while modeling dependencies among grounding decisions. The experiments are on natural-image grounding, so the method is transfer evidence for document-region grounding rather than direct evidence about documents.

title: Scene-Text Oriented Referring Expression Comprehension
abstract: Studies referring-expression grounding in images where scene text is important for identifying the referenced region. The task is transferable to screenshots and document surfaces because successful grounding depends on jointly interpreting text and visual location.

title: ColPali: Efficient Document Retrieval with Vision Language Models
abstract: Represents document pages directly with a vision-language model and performs late-interaction retrieval over their visual contents. It preserves more page-level visual information than text-only indexing, but retrieval is supporting evidence and does not provide precise cell- or region-level grounding by itself.

title: Figure and caption extraction from biomedical documents
abstract: Studies extraction and association of figures and their captions from biomedical documents. The capability is relevant to retaining figure-caption relationships and source locations rather than reducing documents to plain text.

title: Beyond Captions: Linking Figures with Abstract Sentences in Biomedical Articles
abstract: Links scientific figures with textual sentences that describe or discuss them beyond the immediate caption. The work is transferable to resolving references between attachment prose and embedded visual content.

title: Semantic Text Matching for Long-Form Documents
abstract: Studies semantic matching for long documents and includes email attachment suggestion as an application. It provides direct evidence that email context can be matched semantically to attachment content, but the method is text-oriented and does not establish multimodal region-level grounding.

title: Leveraging personal metadata for Desktop search: The Beagle++ system
abstract: Uses personal and contextual metadata to improve desktop search, including relationships between email messages and documents associated with them. It is supporting evidence for retaining email-to-attachment context, rather than evidence for multimodal document understanding or precise source grounding.
